A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Motion-Aware Animatable Gaussian Avatars Deblurring. All pages, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction experiments on synthetic and captured data, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, robustness tests, and qualitative demonstrations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 2–14 and the qualitative reconstruction and animation demonstrations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same blur formation model, B-spline pose interpolation, pose deformation CNN, temporal regularization, shape and skinning refinement, and optimization loss. Diffusion-based refinement is mentioned only as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six ZJU-MoCap subjects, eight-scene captured dataset, AMASS poses, and iPhone demonstration. The blur, view-count, initialization, and mask scenarios are retained. The added low-light discussion introduces no evaluated dataset or scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 2, 10, and 13 retain GauHuman and the ShiftNet, RVRT, VRT, and BSST pipelines combined with GauHuman. Figure 13 retains its GauHuman and BSST-plus-GauHuman comparisons. Added citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The subject and camera splits, RIFE interpolation, capture settings, input resolutions, optimizer settings, and cropped PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS evaluation are unchanged. The parameter sweeps and testing procedures also match.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component and temporal-regularization ablations, trajectory comparisons, control-knot and rendering-sample sweeps, and robustness analyses of SMPL initialization, blur magnitude, view count, and masks. No additional analysis accompanies the new limitations sentences.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. The statistical reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2–14 retain their numerical entries and findings. For example, Table 2 reports the proposed method's PSNR as 25.546 on synthetic data and 27.010 on real data in both versions. The qualitative examples and findings are also retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11), including the blur formulation, interpolation matrix, temporal regularizer, and loss, remain mathematically equivalent. No new definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the claims of direct sharp avatar reconstruction, joint motion/avatar optimization, benchmark creation, and superiority over the evaluated baselines. Removing 'and robustness' from the abstract does not materially narrow the robustness claim retained in the introduction and experiments.

C2.justification: Section 4.5.2 adds a specific limitation connecting sRGB processing to difficulties under low-light degradation and suggests diffusion priors for future avatar refinement. Existing interpretations and limitations concerning geometry, radiance integration, loose garments, and handheld objects remain.

D1.justification: v4 adds 'Codes Available' and a MAD-Avatar repository link in the abstract; v2 only promises future code and dataset release. The future-release sentence remains in v4's introduction. Implementation details are unchanged, and repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 adds references supporting the low-light and diffusion discussions, including NeRF in the Dark, 3DGS-Enhancer, and Difix3D+, and adds RS-NeRF to the interpolation citations. The standalone EasyMocap reference is removed. These are limited literature changes; the central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized abstract and introductory-footnote edits, adds two limitations/future-work sentences and an acknowledgment, and updates bibliography formatting. The section sequence and most explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 moves from page 4 to page 5, with accompanying figure placement, spacing, and text reflow adjustments. The figures and tables retain their examples, comparison structure, and captions; there is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves resource discoverability through its explicit code link and scope disclosure through the low-light caveat in Section 4.5.2. These documentation gains leave the method and experimental evidence unchanged. The PDFs do not verify repository usability or experimentally substantiate the added low-light discussion.
